question: How do you handle eBilling and A/R?
html:
We support law-firm eBilling and accounts receivable, and over roughly the next one to three years we plan to build that into a dedicated billing-and-collections service. The growth plan schedules this work for months 12-30, about Oct 2027 to Apr 2029 (est.) (Frontline growth plan).

Why billing needs attention now

  • Client-side AI is reviewing more law-firm invoices.
  • Invoice rejections have risen from 11% to 18% as a result (Frontline growth plan).
  • More rejections mean more rework and slower payment. That is the gap we intend to close.

How we will build it

ElementWhat the growth plan says
ScopeBring eBilling and A/R together as one service
CapacityAdd specialist billing firms through acquisition
Acquisition screenIncludes Helm360, The Garver Group and The Legal Billing Group
AutomationFour finance AI agents
PricingTied to days-to-pay, not just effort
InternationalAccurate Legal Billing is on the UK and Canada screen (months 24-42)

(Frontline growth plan)

What is not yet defined

  • The context does not say which tasks each of the four finance agents will handle. A service design document or agent specification would answer that.
  • It does not give current eBilling client counts, rejection rates for our own clients, or days-to-pay baselines. Client billing data from the past year would set those baselines.
  • Acquisitions on the screen are candidates only. No deals are confirmed.

For firms considering us

  • If rejections or slow payments are a problem today, our current team can review your billing workflow.
  • As the dedicated service launches, pricing on days-to-pay means our fee is tied to how quickly you get paid.

BSP's investment carried a $90M term loan at an est. 12-15x entry multiple, so EBITDA growth has to carry the return. The roadmap counts on about $25M of acquired MSP and billing-services revenue by month 24 (est.). Outcome-priced billing work is one of the clearest routes to that growth (Frontline public filings; Frontline growth plan).

Next actions for the operating team

  1. Pull 12 months of rejection-rate and days-to-pay data for current billing clients to set the pricing baseline.
  2. Write the specification for the four finance agents, with a target metric for each.
  3. Rank Helm360, The Garver Group and The Legal Billing Group on revenue, client overlap and fit before month 12.
  4. Draft a days-to-pay pricing model and test it with two or three existing law-firm clients.
